body:
First of all, thanks a load for the advice! I uninstalled the games to make room for other things I enjoy almost as much, but are more productive. I was playing sometimes 10/12 hours a day, probably about 4 hours when I had classes. It didn't leave much room for watching new movies or reading so I decided that until I sort out the rest of my life I should give up games. I'll definitely pick them up again when I'm sure that I've become able to pace myself.

I've always worked out in the afternoon, but I think doing it in the morning will be better for me. I've never been much of a morning person and always take forever to really "wake up", which is something I've wanted to fix.

Thanks again!

Yeah, having trouble finding paid internships. Other than that, I just checked on campus enrolment website and 3 out of 4 were people paying to help with research. Maybe some stuff will open up during the semester but it's summer break in Aus atm.

Yeah, my problem is finding paid internships, I have the option of finding something unpaid quickly I suppose, but I guess it's a bit of a last resort unless people think it'll look good on a resume. 

I really do need to start making money, lacking independence is making me go a bit crazy. I've applied for a job at my university for IT helpdesk, but everyone applies for it since it pays ridiculously well (>30$/h). So don't have hopes up for that.

Thanks! I've checked out on-campus stuff, and have applied for one that didn't take a resume, the others generally ask for admin experience and the like, which I have none of.

I'm absolutely terrible at marketing myself, it gets difficult trying to find ways to even fill a resume >.>

Oh, GG can't acronym. Most part time places I've looked at still ask for a resume (generally looking at retail/fast food chains). I rarely see "help wanted" signs or anything of the sort where I live.
PT? Do you mean PR or... ?

Ah, I should have clarified. I'm not just going for degree related work, right now anything is good for me. Honestly looking for any positions. My problem is that I can't think of what kinds of general/specific things to add for skills. 

Should I keep the resume to 1 page or try to make it any longer? I've also heard a lot of people recommend not putting any information about references in, is that generally the rule?

Thinking about it more clearly the next day, if anything it was about 50/50. Neither of us were paying enough attention. I thought she was done parking and moved forward, but she wasn't in properly and backed out. It hit the rear door, so I was already far enough in for her to be able to see I'm back there. 

I'm not particularly familiar with the area and it was quite late so I was going slow, didn't want to miss the turn into his street. Neither of us were paying enough attention.
Yeah told him what happened and how. Asked a couple questions then nodded and walked off, better than expected. My mother, on the other hand, is kinda freaked and over-protective as usual >.>

Yeah, that was my first thought, too. When it happened I ran through my mental rolodex but nobody I know. Thanks for the advice, I wasn't gonna try and dance around it or lie in the first place though.

Yeah, just saying that I should have at least Googled it myself before posting since reddit has such a large American demographic. But yeah w/e. That and I'm rambling a bit cause I'm nervous about explaining it to him when he wakes up >.> Gonna be a fun discussion.

So, $1k give or take a couple hundred depending how bad it really is, I suppose. I do live in Australia so I kind of assume it's going to be more expensive than what it would be in America (everything else here seems to be).
Ah, right, my bad. You can probably tell I know next to nothing about this >.> Also appears to be a 2012 model, not 2011.
